Title: The Unraveling

INT. PSYCHIATRIC WARD - NIGHT

The dimly lit room is filled with the sound of distant screams. A young woman, JESSICA, sits on her bed, her eyes wide with fear. A nurse, MRS. BAKER, enters.

MRS. BAKER
(Gently)
Jessica, it's time for your medication.

JESSICA
(Whispering)
I don't want it. I don't want to be here.

Mrs. Baker sits next to her.

MRS. BAKER
I know this is hard, but you're not alone. We're here to help you.

INT. PSYCHIATRIC WARD - THE NEXT DAY

Jessica stands in front of the mirror, staring at her reflection. She touches her face, as if trying to remember who she was before this place.

Suddenly, she hears a voice in her head.

VOICE (V.O.)
You're not really Jessica, you know.

INT. CAFETERIA - DAY

Jessica sits alone at a table, eating her lunch. A man, THOMAS, approaches her.

THOMAS
(Smiling)
Mind if I join you?

Jessica looks up, her eyes filled with fear, but she nods. Thomas takes a seat across from her.

THOMAS
You seem troubled. Can I help in some way?

Jessica hesitates, then begins to tell him about the voice in her head. Thomas listens intently.

THOMAS
That's a common symptom of dissociative identity disorder. It's important to remember that you're not alone in this.

INT. PSYCHIATRIC WARD - NIGHT

Jessica lies in bed, awake, as the voice grows louder in her head.

VOICE (V.O.)
You're not really Jessica. You're so much more than that.

Jessica sits up, her eyes wide with terror.

JESSICA
(Screaming)
Who are you?!

INT. PSYCHIATRIC WARD - THE NEXT DAY

Jessica stands in front of a group of fellow patients, sharing her story. They listen intently, some with sympathy, others with fear. Thomas sits in the back, observing.

JESSICA
I used to think I was crazy, but now I realize that this voice is a part of me. I'm not just Jessica, I'm a collection of experiences and emotions, and that's okay.

INT. PSYCHIATRIC WARD - LATER

Jessica sits in a therapy session, talking with her doctor about her progress.

DOCTOR
You've come a long way, Jessica. You've learned to accept and embrace all parts of yourself.

Jessica nods, a small smile on her face.

JESSICA
I'm not crazy, I'm complex.

INT. PSYCHIATRIC WARD - NIGHT

Jessica lies in bed, the voice in her head now a comforting presence.

VOICE (V.O.)
You're not really Jessica, but that's okay. You're so much more than just one identity.

Jessica closes her eyes, a sense of peace washing over her.

FADE OUT.

---

END OF SCREENPLAY.
